S1.rationale: A typed hosted Agent run makes repeated model decisions and executes first-party tools/delegation until completion or bounded interruption; checkpoints and tool results return operational evidence. No specific S1 bug with measured impact is identified by this assessment.

S2.rationale: INLINE/TASK delegates, root-shared limits, graph snapshots and workflow dependency edges constrain call-tree growth and task order, not a demonstrated feedback response to interference among independent S1 units. No native overlap incident or coordination demand is evidenced.

S3.rationale: The management plane publishes versioned Agents/Tools/Workflows, while runtime cancellation/leases/quotas control runs; no agent has a live whole-installation view and intervenes across competing obligations. Missing S3 classification is not a requirement for a second control plane.

S3*.rationale: Rich run and delegation audit rows, traces and admin UI expose facts but do not independently adjudicate claim correctness and feed corrective obligations. Without a concrete false-report or audit defect, this is a viable hypothesis area only, not a product-specific proposed patch.

S4.rationale: Operators draft, test and publish capabilities, and runs retain state, but no first-party autonomous actor develops outside/future alternatives and adopts them into active service. The assessment cannot support an unsolicited prospective adaptation module.

S5.rationale: RBAC, AAP grants, workspace scopes, publication rights and A2A auth enforce externally defined permissions. No legitimate native identity-level policy owner is established or shown needed for a bounded change in this installation.
